messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 page - routing/compliance: Detected routing policy violation for customer=finlytics. Data residency=US but 1.2k requests (approx) routed to eu-west-1 between 1710758340-1710758460. Possible fallback loop after model-variant mismatch. Paging @oncall. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/data-residency

Mia Chen: I'm seeing the same in the router logs. sample: `customer=finlytics request_id=7a3f selected_region=eu-west-1 original_region=us-west-2 policy=enforce_residency=US fallback_taken=true model_variant=redwood-3b-quant`

Raj Patel: quick glance at smart-routing config - the fallback policy for region_priority is empty for this customer group. Looks like we allowed "prefer_lower_cost" fallback which routed to eu when capacity missing in us. This should have been blocked by residency policy enforcement.

Leah Ortiz: tagging @Security Bot and @Priya (Legal) — CS is prepping the customer note but need impact details ASAP. Ana (CS) is standing by to send a heads-up if we confirm exfiltration risk = none.

Oncall Rob: I'm paged, taking lead. Steps: 1) suspend cross-region fallback for finlytics 2) pin routing to us-west-2 3) escalate to security if data left region. Will post commands I run.

Raj Patel: reproducing config problem locally. The per-customer policy merge code is erroneously allowing the global fallback policy to override residency when a model variant mismatch occurs. Suspect recent change in commit `c4a9f1` (smart-routing default merge). Snippet of offending rule from DB:```json
{"customer_id":"finlytics","residency":"US","fallback_policy":{"prefer_lower_cost":true,"allowed_regions":[]}}
```

Mia Chen: logs show a small loop: request retried -> target eu node returns incompatible model variant -> fallback kicks to eu -> retry again. That creates a few hundred routed tokens before we detect. No evidence yet that payload content left the customer tenant beyond routing.

Security Bot: Flagged as COMPLIANCE-PRIO. Collecting audit trails: routing decisions, timestamps, model_variant hashes. If any PII left non-US storage we treat as data residency violation and escalate to SEC001.

Oncall Rob: executing mitigation (patching routing config):
```
# patch: disable cross-region fallback for customer finlytics
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://api.redwood.internal/configs/routing/pin -d '{"customer_id":"finlytics","pin_region":"us-west-2","disable_cross_region_fallback":true}'
```
Applying now...

Mia Chen: Noted. Also temporarily increasing retry_backoff to avoid rapid loops: `retry_backoff_ms=2000` for the finlytics policy.

Oncall Rob: Patch applied. Restarting routing-proxy for immediate pickup: `kubectl -n routing rollout restart deploy/router-proxy`

Raj Patel: After restart, new logs show selected_region=us-west-2 for new requests. Sample: `request_id=9b2d selected_region=us-west-2 policy=enforce_residency=US fallback_taken=false`

Ana (CS): Confirmed with customer rep on support call: they saw increased latency and a few failed requests, but no confirmed data leakage. CS will send the initial incident notification and a short FAQ.

Priya (Legal): Need an impact summary within 30m: number of unique requests routed out-of-region, any persisted data in eu-west-1 (logs, KV cache), and whether model artifacts with customer data were cached there.

Mia Chen: Quick numbers: ~1,200 requests, ~14k tokens, window ~2 minutes. No persisted KV cache entries observed for finlytics keys on eu nodes (checked cache::list for `finlytics:*` — empty). Logs show ephemeral KV allocations only.

Security Bot: audit bundle created: s3://incidents-audit/1710758400-finlytics-routing-bundle.tar.gz. Marked for SEC triage.

Leah Ortiz: Opening incident ticket INC-2026-234 with owners: @Oncall Rob (lead), @Raj (root cause), @Mia (validation), @Ana (customer comms). Postmortem slot scheduled EOD.

Oncall Rob: Moving to stabilize -> monitor. Setting alert to 5xx and any cross-region routing spikes. Also adding a temporary rule to block auto-fallback to eu regions for all customers with residency != EU.

Raj Patel: Root cause summary for now: policy-merge bug allowed empty allowed_regions to be treated as "any" combined with prefer_lower_cost fallback. Fix will be a validation guard in the policy-merge step + unit test. Planning patch and release tomorrow.

Priya (Legal): Good. Please include timestamps/IDs for audit and a short description for breach register if needed. I'll review CS note before send.

Ana (CS): Draft sent to Priya, cc'ing customer. Will wait for final wording.

Mia Chen: Closing mitigation thread. We'll keep monitoring for 1 hour. If no further cross-region routes seen, downgrade to Sev3 and start postmortem.

Security Bot: Marking incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Next: forensic check scheduled.

Oncall Rob: Thanks all — assigning follow-ups and handing to the day oncall. Leaving a short handoff note in #eng-oncall.

Leah Ortiz: Follow-ups: code fix (Raj), add validation test (Mia), postmortem draft (Leah), customer follow-up (Ana), legal review (Priya).

incident-bot: incident INC-2026-234 created and linked: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-234
